thread.title: Stock Market Update: U.S. Futures Tumble, Apple Revenue Guidance Cut Weighs on Sentiment

title: Stock Market Update: U.S. Futures Tumble, Apple Revenue Guidance Cut Weighs on Sentiment
text:
U.S. Futures Tumble, Apple Revenue Guidance Cut Weighs on Sentiment 03-Jan-19 07:56 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: -34.40. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: -136.50.
U.S. futures point to another sharply lower open after Apple (AAPL 144.92, -13.00, -8.2%) cut its revenue guidance for the first time since 2002. The S&P 500 futures trade 34 points, or 1.4%, below fair value a day after stocks overcame early losses to edge higher.
Specifically, Apple lowered its Q1 fiscal revenue guidance to $84 billion from the previously forecast range of $89-$93 billion. CEO Tim Cook, in a CNBC interview, said the shortfall is solely due to weaker-than-expected iPhone revenue, primarily in Greater China. Mr. Cook added that he believes trade tensions between the United States and China have put additional pressure on China's economy.
Longer-dated U.S. Treasuries have extended their gains, pressuring yields. The benchmark 10-yr yield is down two basis points to 2.64%. The U.S. Dollar Index is down 0.2%, and WTI crude is up 0.3% to $46.67/bbl.
On the data front, investors will receive several economic reports today: the ADP Employment Change report for December (Briefing.com consensus 170,000) at 8:15 a.m. ET; weekly Initial Claims (Briefing.com consensus 220,000) and Continuing Claims at 8:30 a.m. ET; the ISM Manufacturing Index for December (Briefing.com consensus 57.8) at 10:00 a.m. ET; and auto and truck sales throughout the day.
Earlier, the weekly MBA Mortgage Applications Index decreased 8.5%, which is lower than the decrease of 5.8% from two weeks ago.
In U.S. Corporate news: Apple (AAPL 144.92, -13.00): -8.2% after the company lowered its Q1 fiscal revenue guidance, citing lower-than-expected iPhone revenue, primarily in Greater China. Celgene (CELG 87.04, +20.40): +30.8% after agreeing to be acquired by Bristol-Myers (BMY 44.55, -7.88, -15.0%) for $102.43/share, or roughly $74 billion, and one CVR per share.
Reviewing overnight developments: Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region ended Thursday on a mixed note while Japan's Nikkei remained closed. Hong Kong's Hang Seng -0.3%, China's Shanghai Composite UNCH, India's Sensex -1.1%, South Korea's Kospi -0.8%, Australia's ASX All Ordinaries +1.2%. In economic data: Hong Kong's November Retail Sales +1.4% year-over-year (last 5.9%) New Zealand's GDT Price Index 2.8% (last 1.7%) In news: Apple suppliers listed in Hong Kong underperformed after the tech giant lowered its revenue guidance for the first time since 2002, citing weakness in China. On a related note, Korean press reported that Samsung will cut its chip inventory due to a supply glut. The foreign exchange market saw some volatility during its least-liquid time. The Japanese yen jumped from 110 against the dollar to 105, before trimming its advance. The Australian dollar briefly retreated to 0.6744 against the dollar before narrowing its loss to 0.4% at 0.6957. Major European indices trade in negative territory. STOXX Europe 600 -0.9%, Germany's DAX -1.3%, UK's FTSE 100 -0.4%, France's CAC 40 -1.2%, Italy's FTSE MIB -0.6%, Spain's IBEX 35 -0.1%. In news: Apple's revenue guidance cut has weighed on sentiment while also pressuring European chipmakers like STMicroelectronics (-9.5%) and Infineon (-5.1%). British Prime Minister Theresa May is expected to meet with European officials, including EU Council President Donald Tusk, German Chancellor Angela Merkel, and Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte. Ms. May will seek to secure concessions regarding the Irish border ahead of the Brexit withdrawal bill expected during the week of January 14. In economic data: Eurozone November M3 Money Supply +3.7% year-over-year (expected 3.8%; last 3.9%) and Private Sector Loans +3.3% year-over-year, as expected (last 3.2%) UK's December Construction PMI 52.8 (expected 52.9; last 53.4) Spain's December Unemployment Change -50,600 (last -1,800) and December Consumer Confidence 90.9 (last 91.4) Swiss December SVME PMI 57.8 (expected 57.0; last 57.7) Add this to my Page Alerts .
